Subject: Initial pricing ask for Veridian private deployment

Hi Monica / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran this by the procurement and infra teams and they asked for a clearer view on a couple of points before we escalate to legal:

1) How does Redwood structure the platform fee for a private VPC deployment vs node/operator licensing? We need an example for a 3-site deployment.
2) What support tiers look like (Response times, credits) and whether SRE retainer hours can be purchased as a month-by-month add-on.

Cheers,

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the clear list. Im looping in Marissa and David to provide the commercial and SLA detail; Irene will weigh in on SRE retainer options and migration credit mechanics.

High-level preview so you have something to share with procurement ASAP:
- Platform fee: fixed annual platform fee that covers control-plane, observability, and security integrations. For a 3-site pilot we typically recommend the Starter Platform tier (covers up to 3 sites).
- Operator license: per-site operator license that maps to on-prem/site management; optional per-node SKU for large GPU clusters.
- Support tiers: Standard (8x5, P1 4h), Business (24x7, P1 1h) and Enterprise (24x7 with SRE retainer). Credits for SLA misses scale by severity.
- Migration credit: we can offer a one-time pilot migration credit — proposal below from Marissa.

Ill send a short term sheet with numbers in the next message.

Best,
Monica
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Initial pricing ask for Veridian private deployment

Elaine / team —

Attached is a concise term sheet (PDF) and a starter SOW. Key commercial bullets (pilot, 12-month view):

- Platform fee (Starter Platform): $55k/year (covers control plane, 90d observability retention, analytics, and security connectors) for up to 3 sites.
- Operator licenses: $6k/site/year (includes operator tooling and on-call routing). For 3 sites = $18k/year.
- Node licensing (optional): $3k/node/year if you want per-GPU billing (only if >8 GPUs/site).
- Support: Business tier recommended for production pilot — $25k/year includes 24x7 monitoring, P1 1h response, P2 4h. Enterprise tier adds a 160h/yr SRE retainer and a dedicated SRE on-call rota.
- Migration/onboarding credit: we can provide a 7% credit on the first-year invoice to offset migration engineering for the pilot (applies to platform fee + operator licenses), plus one month of SRE retainer (one-time) for free to cover cutover.

Notes on SLA credits: P1 downtime credits = 5% of monthly platform fee per incident (capped at 25% monthly). We can flex severity buckets for Enterprise.

Ive labeled the term sheet with line items and included an example invoice schedule. If procurement wants a deeper discount in exchange for a 24-month committed term we can model that — propose we discuss tradeoffs Monday.

Attachments: Veridian_VPC_Termsheet_20261007.pdf, SOW-starter-pilot-attachment.docx

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Questions about platform fee amortization and SLA carveouts

Marissa / Monica —

Quick clarifying questions from procurement/legal:
- Can the platform fee be amortized quarterly instead of annual upfront? We have internal CAPEX constraints.
- On the migration credit: is the 7% absolute or negotiable? Were asking for 10% as an anchor given multi-site complexity.
- For the Enterprise SRE retainer, can you confirm the escalation contact and whether SRE hours roll over month-to-month during the first 6 months?

Also please confirm license transfer rules if we add/remove sites mid-term.

Tom Park
Sr. Manager, Procurement
Veridian Health
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Park <t.park@veridianhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Torres <elaine@veridianhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions about platform fee amortization and SLA carveouts

Tom —

Answers inline: 
- Amortization: We can offer quarterly invoicing with a 3% payment processing surcharge for non-annual prepay. If you prefer a term-commit (24 months) we can convert to monthly billing with no surcharge but require minimum quarterly invoicing.
- Migration credit: Marissa initially proposed 7%. If Veridian signs a 24-month committed term we can increase to 10% on year-one charges (platform + operator licenses). For a 12-month pilot term the 7% stands.
- SRE retainer: escalation contact is the Enterprise SRE team (sre-enterprise@redwood.com) and a named lead will be provided in the SOW. Hours do not roll over month-to-month in the first 6 months; they are pooled against the annual retainer. We can provide a one-month free retainer during pilot as a gesture (as noted).
- License transfers: operator licenses are transferrable between sites once per contract year with a small administrative fee ($500/event). Node SKUs are flexible but must be declared at quarter boundaries for billing.

If youd like, Marissa and Monica can put the 24-month tradeoff on paper (discount vs amortization) and send a redline-friendly term sheet.

Regards,
David
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Elaine / Tom —

Appreciate the visibility into procurements constraints. Based on Davids notes, heres a short set of options for your review: 

Option A — 12-month pilot (no long-term commit)
- Platform fee: $55k/year, invoiced quarterly with 3% surcharge
- Operator licenses: $6k/site/year (3 sites = $18k), billed quarterly
- Migration credit: 7% applied to first-year charges
- SRE: one month free of the 160h annual retainer included as a pilot concession

Option B — 24-month commitment (preferred for deeper discount)
- Platform fee: $50k/year (9% discount applied across term), invoiced monthly (no surcharge)
- Operator licenses: $5.4k/site/year (10% discount)
- Migration credit: 10% on year-one charges
- SRE: 160h/year retainer included at $0 for month 1, and 20% discount on additional SRE hours for year 1

Other contractual items:
- Admin fee for site transfer: $500/event
- SLA credits: as previously described; Enterprise can have custom buckets in SOW

Next steps: If youd like Option B, well prepare a draft term sheet and redline-friendly SOW and share the DocuSign link for signature. If you prefer Option A, we can send the single-year agreement and pilot SOW.

Ill follow up with the term sheet attachments (attached here) and a HubSpot deal update after you tell me which direction you prefer.

Thanks,
Monica
Director, Strategic Sales
